design:
D1. The link is content, carried in the change's payload, not a database column. It is validated on save and survives every submission, like `roadmap`. It needs no migration, so this is Tier 1. Rejected: a link table, because it would let the link and the document disagree, and the document is the source.

D2. The waiting lists are computed from the parsed documents the spec lists already reuse (commit cda8adb, spec-list-cost), plus spec_document_merges to tell which changes are folded. Rejected: a stored reverse index, which would have to be kept in step on every save, fold and archive.

D3. An author may change the link only while exploring, because an approved document refuses submissions. After approval, the operator changes it through a route, and a spec-admin agent through a new tidy op. Neither changes requirement digests, so approval stands.

D4. The fold keeps every choice it has today. Only its starting target changes; an off-link fold is allowed and recorded.

LESSONS FROM SLICE 1, applied here:
- The drive and the UI disagreed on element names (AOTCT-4, evidence for FR-1/6/10/13 rejected). The test ids below are part of the contract, and the drive asserts only these.
- A list ordered by wall clock was random within a tick (AOTCT-2). Every list here names a total order, and ties on a timestamp fall back to insertion order before anything else (vault fact fct-094e0ecc1706).

CONTRACT:
- Payload field on change-spec: `capabilities: {"changes": [<capability path>], "creates": [{"title": str}]}`. It is optional; absent means none.
- Submission refusal code `capability_unknown`. Warning code `capability_unnamed`.
- Capability read: `waiting_changes: [{path, title, phase, built: bool, first_approved_at | null}]`, ordered by first_approved_at ascending with nulls last, then by the document's creation order (insertion order, not a timestamp), then path.
- Change read: `folded_into: <capability path> | null`.
- read_spec_document accepts `include=waiting` on a capability.
- Operator route: `PUT /documents/{path}/capabilities` with body {changes, creates, reason}. It returns the document, or 409 with `change_folded`.
- Spec list rows for capabilities carry `waiting_count`.
- Tidy op `set_capabilities(path, changes, creates, reason)`. The tidy op `fold` with no `capability` uses the single named capability, or refuses with `capability_ambiguous` (several named) or `capability_unnamed` (none named).
- The fold record carries `fold_target_not_named: true` when the target is not named.
- UI test ids:
  - On a change's page: `change-capabilities` (the named list), `change-capabilities-edit`.
  - On a capability's page: `capability-waiting-list`, whose rows are `capability-waiting-row` with `data-path` and `data-built`.
  - On the spec list: `capability-waiting-count`.
  - In the fold dialog: `fold-target` (its value is the selected path) and `fold-create-named`.

GUARDS: none relaxed. Existing fold tests keep passing because a change with no link falls back to today's picker.

lifecycle: Ships as slice 2 of 'The specs stay true and easy to work with'. Once built, the spec-admin agent names the capability of this repository's unfolded changes, which slice 3 then folds automatically.
problem: A change says which capability it changes only at the moment it is folded, when FoldIntoCapabilityDialog.tsx:53 offers every capability in the project to pick from. On this repository only 14 of 165 changes mention a capability at all. Nobody can ask which open changes affect capability X, and every fold begins with a hunt for its target. That is part of why the 48 built changes stayed unfolded. Slice 1 (an-agent-the-operator-trusts-can-tidy-the-specs, merged on master) gave a trusted agent the power to fold. This slice gives each fold a target it can read rather than guess.

requirements.statement: A change document can name zero or more existing capabilities it changes and zero or more new capabilities it will create, each new one by title. The names are part of the document's content, are shown on the change's page, and survive every later submission that carries them.

requirements.rationale: A link to nothing would put a change on no capability's waiting list and fail silently at fold time.
requirements.statement: A submission naming a path that is not a current capability of the same project is refused, naming the path, and the document is unchanged.

requirements.rationale: Approvals are scarce: warn, do not gate (operator, 2026-10-08). Some changes, like a test-only fix, change no capability.
requirements.statement: A change that names no capability, existing or new, draws a warning on submission and at approval, and is never blocked by it.

The named capabilities can be changed until the change is folded or archived: by an author's submission while the document is exploring, by the operator at any phase, and by an agent with the spec-admin switch as a tidy act with a reason. A change to the link on an approved document does not alter its requirements or reopen it. After a fold the link is fixed.

requirements.rationale: Slice 1's tidy list failed review because acts in the same clock tick came back in random order. Every list this slice adds names a total order. The clock ticks only about every 15 ms on Windows, so an 'oldest first' list falls back to the order the records were created before anything else (vault fact fct-094e0ecc1706); the path is only the last resort.
requirements.statement: Each capability lists the changes that name it and are neither folded nor archived. Each entry shows the change's title, phase, and whether every one of its tasks is approved. Entries are ordered by first approval, oldest first, with changes never approved after them. Changes that tie are ordered by which was created first, and the path breaks any tie that remains.
The operator can see, for every capability in a project, how many open changes name it, and open the list. An agent can read the same list with read_spec_document on the capability.

Folding a change that names exactly one existing capability opens with that capability as the target, both in the operator's fold dialog and in the agent's tidy fold when no capability is given. A change naming several asks which; a change naming a new capability offers to create it with the named title. Folding into a capability the change does not name is allowed, and the fold's record says so.
Once folded, a change leaves every waiting list and shows which capability it was folded into. Changes folded before this slice show the capability recorded by their fold.
The link, the waiting lists and the default fold target behave the same in every project, with no dependence on this repository's layout.

in_scope: A field on a change document naming the existing capabilities it changes, and any new capability it will create
Validation of the named capabilities on submission, and a warning when a change names none
Changing the link while the change is not yet folded, by its authors, the operator, or a spec-admin agent
A list on each capability of the changes naming it that are not yet folded or archived
A view of which open changes affect any capability, for the operator in the app and for agents through read_spec_document
The fold (operator dialog and agent tidy fold) defaulting to the named capability
non_goals: Guessing the capability of existing changes automatically; the spec-admin agent sets them as tidy acts
Folding automatically when a build finishes (slice a-finished-build-folds-itself)
Moving files on disk or changing the index layout (slice live-apart-from-finished)
Blocking approval of a change that names no capability: it warns

summary: A change document names, while it is being written, the existing capabilities it changes and any new capability it will create. Each capability then lists the changes waiting to fold into it. The operator and agents can see which open changes affect any capability. A fold starts from the named capability instead of a search.
